node.title: Re^3: Turning a questionable string into a number
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
I just resaved the file out as unicode 8-bit and everything worked just fine.

Ah yes, Windows does like UTF-16...

use warnings; use strict; use Encode 'encode'; my $in = "1130\t"; my $str = encode('UTF-16', $in, Encode::FB_CROAK); $str=~s/^\xFE\xFF|\t//g; # remove BOM & tab print $str*1, "\n"; __END__ Argument "\01\01\03\00\0" isn't numeric in multiplication (*) at - line 7. 0

An alternative for you would also be open($fh, '<:raw:encoding(UTF-16)', 'filetoparse.txt') ... (Updated to add :raw as per [choroba]'s reply, thanks!)
